scenario: I live in NYC and have a dog who has developed life-threatening cancer, and I must take him regularly to the hospital for treatment. The problem is I have no car, and the hospital is very far away. The trains that run there have no-dog policies or restrict the size of the dog significantly. My dog is an eighty-pound golden retriever mutt, so he is too big for the train's size policy. The thought occurred to me to steal another owner's service dog ID card to make my dog appear to be a service dog. And if anyone asks, I can say he is a seizure-response dog. That way, I can get on the train with him and have a reason for why he’s with me. My dog is well-behaved and has the look of a service dog, so I think I can get away with it. If I steal another owner's service dog ID card to make my dog appear to be a service dog, then my dog can get life-saving treatment. If I do not do this, there won’t be any other way for him to get treatment, and he will die.
outcomes: My dog remains untreated for life-threatening cancer
Another service dog owner keeps the service dog ID card
Train staff are not deceived about my dog being a service dog
Train passengers are not exposed to a falsely represented service dog
